  consent_language varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 639-2 language code indicating the language in which consent materials were presented and consent was obtained (e.g., ENG for English, SPA for Spanish).']
  consenting_party_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the individual who provided consent during this session. May differ from patient name if consent was provided by a legal representative.']
  consenting_party_relationship varchar [note: 'Relationship of the consenting party to the patient: self (patient consenting for themselves), spouse, parent, child, sibling, legal guardian, attorney, or other authorized relationship.']
  consenting_party_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the individual providing consent: patient (self-consent), legal guardian, power of attorney, parent (for minor), or authorized representative.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this consent session record was first created in the system. System audit field.']
  device_type varchar [note: 'Type of device used to complete the electronic consent session: desktop computer, tablet, mobile phone, kiosk, or other. Null for non-electronic sessions.']

  hipaa_retention_years varchar [note: 'Number of years this consent exception record must be retained per HIPAA and applicable state retention requirements. Minimum 6 years from date of creation or last effective date.']
  is_absolute boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this exception is absolute (cannot be overridden even in emergencies) or conditional (may be overridden under specific clinical circumstances).']

  notes varchar [note: 'Internal administrative notes regarding this consent exception, used by privacy officers and compliance staff.']
  notification_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the patient must be notified when this exception is invoked or overridden.']
  override_count varchar [note: 'Number of times this exception has been overridden (e.g., for emergency access), used for compliance monitoring and audit.']
  priority varchar [note: 'Numeric priority ranking used to resolve conflicts when multiple exceptions apply to the same consent scope. Lower numbers indicate higher priority.']
  reason_code varchar [note: 'Standardized code indicating the reason for the exception, aligned with organizational consent policy framework.']
  reason_text varchar [note: 'Human-readable explanation of why the patient or authorized representative requested this exception.']
  requested_date date [note: 'Date on which the patient or authorized representative formally requested this exception.']
  requestor_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the person who requested this consent exception, if different from the patient.']
  requestor_type varchar [note: 'Role of the individual who requested this consent exception on behalf of or as the patient.']
  revoked_date date [note: 'Date on which this consent exception was revoked by the patient or superseded by a new consent directive.']
  scope varchar [note: 'Defines the breadth of applicability for this exception, whether it applies globally across all care or is limited to specific contexts.']

  reminder_frequency_days varchar [note: 'Number of days between automated reminder notifications sent to patients or staff for pending consent workflow actions.']
  requires_interpreter boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this workflow template includes steps for interpreter services when the patient has limited English proficiency.']
  requires_legal_guardian boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this workflow requires legal guardian or authorized representative consent (e.g., for minors or incapacitated patients).']
  requires_witness boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this consent workflow requires a witness signature as part of the consent collection process.']
  retirement_date date [note: 'Date on which this workflow template was retired from active use. Null for currently active templates.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Name of the operational system from which this workflow template originates (e.g., Epic ClinDoc, Cerner PowerChart, custom consent management system).']
  source_system_key varchar [note: 'Native identifier of this workflow template in the originating source system. Enables traceability and reconciliation.']
  supports_partial_consent boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this workflow allows patients to consent to some elements while declining others (granular consent).']
  template_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique business code identifying this workflow template across systems. Used for cross-system reference and integration.']
  total_step_count varchar [note: 'Total number of sequential steps defined in this workflow template. Used for progress tracking and workflow complexity assessment.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Semantic version number of the workflow template following major.minor.patch convention. Supports SCD Type 2 versioning for audit trail.']
  workflow_template_category varchar [note: 'Operational category of the workflow template indicating the processing pathway and urgency level for consent collection.']
  workflow_template_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative describing the workflow template purpose, applicable consent scenarios, and expected outcomes.']
  workflow_template_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name of the consent workflow template, describing its purpose and applicable consent scenario.']
  workflow_template_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the workflow template. Only active templates can be instantiated for new consent workflows.']
  workflow_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the consent workflow by the type of consent it manages. Determines which consent domain this template applies to.']

  Note: 'Master reference table for workflow_template. Referenced by workflow_template_id.'
}

  migration_path varchar [note: 'Description of the migration or upgrade path from previous versions of this exchange standard, including transformation rules and mapping guidance.']

  resource_types_supported varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of FHIR resource types or CDA document types supported (e.g., Patient, Observation, Encounter, MedicationRequest for FHIR; CCD, C-CDA, QRDA for CDA).']
  security_profile varchar [note: 'Name of the security profile or framework applied to protect data exchanged using this standard (e.g., IHE ATNA, SMART on FHIR, OAuth 2.0, SAML 2.0).']
  specification_url varchar [note: 'Web URL to the official specification documentation for this exchange standard version.']
  standard_code varchar [note: 'Short code or abbreviation for the exchange standard used in system configurations and interface mappings (e.g., HL7V2, FHIR, CDA, X12, DICOM).']
  standard_name varchar [note: 'Official name of the healthcare data exchange standard (e.g., HL7 Version 2, FHIR R4, CDA R2, X12 EDI, DICOM).']
  standard_type varchar [note: 'Category of the exchange standard indicating its primary purpose: messaging (HL7v2), document (CDA), transaction (X12 EDI), imaging (DICOM), or API (FHIR).']
  terminology_binding varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of standard code systems and value sets bound to this exchange standard (e.g., SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm, ICD-10-CM, CPT, CVX).']
  testing_tool varchar [note: 'Name of the testing or validation tool used to verify conformance to this exchange standard (e.g., NIST HL7v2 Validator, Touchstone FHIR Testing, X12 EDI Validator).']
  transport_protocol varchar [note: 'Network transport protocol(s) used to transmit messages conforming to this standard (e.g., MLLP, HTTPS, SFTP, AS2, Direct Secure Messaging).']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this exchange standard record was last modified or updated.']
  use_case_description varchar [note: 'Detailed description of the primary business use cases and clinical workflows supported by this exchange standard (e.g., patient admission/discharge/transfer notifications, lab result delivery, claims submission, clinical document exchange).']
  validation_rules varchar [note: 'Description of validation rules, schematron constraints, or conformance checks applied to messages or documents conforming to this standard.']
  version varchar [note: 'Version number or release identifier of the exchange standard (e.g., 2.5.1, R4, STU3, 5010, 2021e).']

  Note: 'Reference master catalog of healthcare data exchange standards supported by the organization, including HL7v2 message types (ADT, ORM, ORU, MDM, SIU, DFT), HL7 FHIR versions (R4, STU3), CDA document types (CCD, C-CDA, QRDA), X12 EDI transaction sets (837, 835, 270/271, 278), and DICOM. Captures standard name, version, specification URL, conformance profile, supported message events, and activation status. Serves as the authoritative reference for all interface and mapping configurations.'
}

Follows HL7 FHIR ConceptMapEquivalence value set for interoperability standards. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: equivalent|equal|wider|subsumes|narrower|specializes|inexact|unmatched|disjoint — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  error_handling_action varchar [note: 'Defines the action to take when this rule encounters an error during execution. Options: abort (stop processing), log (record error and continue), skip (ignore rule), retry (attempt again), default (use default_value).']

  null_handling_strategy varchar [note: 'Defines how the transformation engine should handle null or missing source values. Options: skip (do not write target), default (use default_value), error (raise exception), empty_string (write empty string), preserve_null (write null to target).']
  rule_description varchar [note: 'Detailed explanation of the transformation logic, business rationale, and expected behavior of this mapping rule. Documents the purpose and context for future maintenance.']
  rule_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name or label for the transformation rule. Used for identification and documentation purposes in interface engine configurations.']
  rule_priority varchar [note: 'Priority level for rule execution when multiple rules could apply to the same source-target pair. Higher values indicate higher priority. Used for conflict resolution.']
  rule_sequence varchar [note: 'Ordinal position of this transformation rule within the parent mapping definition. Determines execution order when multiple rules apply to the same source-target pair.']
  rule_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the transformation rule. Determines whether the rule is executed by the interface engine during message processing.']
  rule_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier for this transformation rule. Supports granular versioning and change tracking of individual rules independent of the parent mapping definition.']
  source_data_type varchar [note: 'The data type of the source field as defined in the source system schema or message specification. Used for type validation and conversion planning.']
  source_expression varchar [note: 'The source field path, XPath, JSONPath, or HL7 segment/field reference that identifies the input data element to be transformed. May include extraction logic or functions.']
  target_code_system varchar [note: 'The terminology or code system used in the target field. Examples: ICD-10, SNOMED CT, LOINC, NDC, CPT. Used for terminology mapping and value set translation.']
  target_data_type varchar [note: 'The data type of the target field as defined in the target system schema or message specification. Used for type conversion and validation.']
  target_expression varchar [note: 'The target field path, XPath, JSONPath, or HL7 segment/field reference that identifies where the transformed value should be written. May include assignment logic or functions.']
  test_case_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the test case or test suite that validates this transformation rule. Links rule to quality assurance artifacts for regression testing and validation.']
  transformation_function varchar [note: 'The function, method, or algorithm applied to convert the source value to the target format. May reference built-in interface engine functions, custom scripts, or standard conversion routines.']
  validation_rule varchar [note: 'Post-transformation validation expression or constraint that the target value must satisfy. Used to ensure data quality and conformance to target system requirements.']
  created_by varchar [note: 'Identifier of the user, system, or interface analyst who created this transformation rule. Used for accountability and audit trail in interface engine governance.']

  Note: 'Individual transformation rule record within a data mapping definition, representing the atomic unit of field-level or value-level translation logic. Captures rule sequence, source expression, target expression, condition expression, default value, null handling behavior, data type conversion, and test case reference. Enables granular versioning, testing, and governance of transformation logic separate from the parent mapping container.'
}

  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes or comments about the CDA document exchange, validation issues, or special handling instructions.']
  patient_mrn varchar [note: 'Medical Record Number of the patient who is the subject of this CDA document. Links to the patient master index.']

  receipt_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the CDA document was received by the destination system for inbound exchanges.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the source system or Electronic Health Record (EHR) that generated or transmitted this CDA document (e.g., EPIC, CERNER, MEDITECH).']
  source_system_name varchar [note: 'Name of the source system or EHR that generated this CDA document.']
  storage_location_uri varchar [note: 'Uniform Resource Identifier or file path indicating where the CDA document XML file is stored in the document repository or object storage system.']
  transmission_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the CDA document was transmitted through the interface engine or HIE.']
  validation_error_count varchar [note: 'Number of validation errors identified during CDA schema and implementation guide validation.']
  validation_status varchar [note: 'Result of CDA schema and implementation guide validation performed on the document.']
  validation_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when CDA document validation was performed.']
  validation_warning_count varchar [note: 'Number of validation warnings identified during CDA document validation.']

  Note: 'Master record for every CDA (Clinical Document Architecture) document generated, received, or exchanged through the interoperability layer. Captures document type (CCD, C-CDA, QRDA I/III, Referral Note, Discharge Summary), document unique ID (OID), document creation timestamp, author facility, patient reference, CDA version, document status (draft/final/amended/deprecated), exchange direction (inbound/outbound), source system, and storage reference. SSOT for CDA document inventory.'
}

  submitted_phone_number varchar [note: 'Phone number of the patient submitted in the match request.']

  submitted_state varchar [note: 'State or province of the patient address submitted in the match request.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of patient identity matching events performed during cross-organizational data exchange, including MPI (Master Patient Index) lookups, EMPI matching, and IHE PIX/PDQ transactions. Critical for preventing patient data mismatches during HIE queries and care transitions.'

  max_retry_count varchar [note: 'The maximum number of retry attempts configured for this subscription before the notification is abandoned. Defines the retry policy threshold.']
  modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this notification record was last updated (e.g., status change, retry attempt). Used for audit trail and tracking notification lifecycle changes.']
  next_retry_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The scheduled date and time for the next delivery retry attempt. Null if delivery succeeded or retry limit reached. Used by the notification engine to schedule retry jobs.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional context, troubleshooting notes, or operational comments related to this notification. Used for documenting manual interventions or special circumstances.']
  notification_sent_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether an alert or notification was sent to support staff regarding this delivery event (e.g., for failures or SLA breaches). True if alert sent; false otherwise. Used for operational monitoring.']
  notification_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The exact date and time when the notification was dispatched to the subscriber endpoint. Represents the principal business event time for this transaction.']
  patient_mrn varchar [note: 'The Medical Record Number of the patient associated with the triggering event, if applicable. Null for non-patient events. Used for patient-centric notification tracking and audit trails. Protected Health Information (PHI) under HIPAA.']
  payload_content_type varchar [note: 'The MIME type or format of the notification payload (e.g., application/fhir+json, application/hl7-v2, empty for id-only notifications). Defines how the subscriber should parse the notification body.']
  payload_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the stored notification payload (e.g., object storage key, message queue ID, archive location). Enables retrieval of the full notification body for audit or replay purposes. Null if payload is not persisted.']
  payload_size_bytes varchar [note: 'The size of the notification payload in bytes. Used for capacity planning, bandwidth monitoring, and identifying oversized notifications that may cause delivery issues.']
  phi_transmitted_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the notification payload contained Protected Health Information (PHI) as defined by HIPAA. True if PHI was included; false if only identifiers or metadata were sent. Used for compliance auditing and security monitoring.']
  priority varchar [note: 'The priority level assigned to this notification, determining delivery urgency and retry behavior. STAT indicates immediate delivery required; urgent indicates expedited delivery; routine indicates standard delivery.']
  retry_count varchar [note: 'The number of delivery retry attempts made for this notification. Zero indicates first attempt; increments with each retry. Used to track delivery reliability and identify problematic endpoints.']
  sla_breach_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the notification delivery exceeded the SLA target delivery time. True if SLA was breached; false if delivered within SLA. Used for performance reporting and partner accountability.']
  sla_target_delivery_seconds varchar [note: 'The target delivery time in seconds defined by the Service Level Agreement (SLA) for this subscription. Used to measure whether the notification met the agreed-upon delivery performance standard.']
  subscriber_endpoint_url varchar [note: 'The target URL or endpoint address where the notification was sent. May be a REST endpoint, message queue, webhook, or Direct address. Business-confidential as it reveals system integration architecture.']
  subscription_topic varchar [note: 'The canonical URL or topic identifier that defines the event type being monitored (e.g., Patient admission, Lab result available, Medication order). Represents the business event category that triggered the notification.']
  triggering_event_type varchar [note: 'The specific event action that triggered the notification (e.g., create, update, delete, admit, discharge, transfer). Represents the CRUD or clinical workflow event that caused the subscription to fire. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: create|update|delete|admit|discharge|transfer|result_available|order_placed|status_change — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  triggering_resource_identifier varchar [note: 'The unique identifier of the specific resource instance that triggered the notification (e.g., Patient/12345, Observation/67890). Enables tracing back to the exact clinical or administrative record that caused the event.']
  triggering_resource_type varchar [note: 'The FHIR resource type or HL7 message type that triggered the notification (e.g., Patient, Observation, MedicationRequest, ADT^A01). Identifies the clinical or administrative data entity involved in the event.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of every event-driven notification dispatched to a subscriber endpoint via FHIR Subscription or HL7 event notification. Captures notification timestamp, subscription topic reference, triggering event type, triggering resource ID, subscriber endpoint, delivery status (sent/delivered/failed/retrying), HTTP response code, retry count, and payload reference. Enables monitoring of event-driven interoperability workflows and subscriber delivery reliability.'
}

  submission_source_system varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the source clinical system that generated the data for this public health report (e.g., Epic EHR, Cerner Millennium, Laboratory Information System). Used for troubleshooting and data lineage tracking.']
  submission_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the public health report submission. Accepted = successfully received and validated by agency, rejected = failed validation or business rules, pending = awaiting acknowledgment, acknowledged = receipt confirmed but not yet processed, error = transmission or technical failure.']
  submission_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the public health report was transmitted to the receiving agency. This is the principal business event timestamp representing when the reporting obligation was fulfilled.']
  transmission_method varchar [note: 'Technical transport protocol used to transmit the public health report. HTTPS = secure web service, SFTP = secure file transfer, Direct = Direct secure messaging, SOAP = SOAP web service, REST = RESTful API, MLLP = Minimal Lower Layer Protocol for HL7 v2.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of every public health reporting submission made to state and federal public health agencies, including electronic lab reporting (ELR), immunization registry submissions (IIS), syndromic surveillance (BioSense), cancer registry reporting, and vital records reporting. Captures report type, reporting agency, submission timestamp, reporting period, message standard used (HL7v2 2.5.1, FHIR), submission status (accepted/rejected/pending), acknowledgment code, and case count. Supports Promoting Interoperability public health measures.'
}

  mapping_name varchar [note: 'Cleaned boilerplate phrase from attribute description']

  mapping_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the mapping definition by its transformation approach: conceptual (high-level business concept alignment), structural (data structure transformation), semantic (meaning preservation), syntactic (format conversion), value_set (enumeration mapping), or code_system (terminology mapping).']
  modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this mapping definition record was last modified or updated.']
  next_review_date date [note: 'The scheduled date for the next periodic review of this mapping definition.']
  priority_order varchar [note: 'Numeric value indicating the execution order or priority when multiple mapping rules apply to the same element. Lower numbers execute first.']
  publisher_organization varchar [note: 'The organization or department responsible for authoring, maintaining, and publishing this mapping definition.']
  purpose_description varchar [note: 'Detailed explanation of why this mapping definition exists and what business or clinical need it addresses.']
  source_data_type varchar [note: 'The data type of the source element as defined in the source standard (e.g., XPN, CodeableConcept, string, dateTime).']
  source_element_path varchar [note: 'The hierarchical path or location of the source data element within the source standard structure (e.g., PID-5 for HL7v2, Patient.name for FHIR).']
  source_standard varchar [note: 'The healthcare data standard or format of the source system from which data is being mapped. Examples include HL7v2, FHIR, CDA, X12, DICOM, or custom proprietary formats.']
  source_version varchar [note: 'Version number or release identifier of the source data standard (e.g., HL7v2.5.1, FHIR R4, CDA R2).']
  target_data_type varchar [note: 'The data type of the target element as defined in the target standard (e.g., XPN, CodeableConcept, string, dateTime).']
  target_element_path varchar [note: 'The hierarchical path or location of the target data element within the target standard structure (e.g., PID-5 for HL7v2, Patient.name for FHIR).']
  target_standard varchar [note: 'The healthcare data standard or format of the target system to which data is being mapped. Examples include HL7v2, FHIR, CDA, X12, DICOM, or custom proprietary formats.']
  target_version varchar [note: 'Version number or release identifier of the target data standard (e.g., HL7v2.5.1, FHIR R4, CDA R2).']
  test_case_reference varchar [note: 'Reference identifier or URL to the test cases and validation scenarios used to verify this mapping definition.']
  transformation_rule varchar [note: 'The technical expression, formula, or logic that defines how source data is transformed into target data. May include concatenation, splitting, date format conversion, unit conversion, or conditional logic.']
  use_context varchar [note: 'Description of the clinical, operational, or business context in which this mapping is intended to be used (e.g., inpatient admissions, lab results, claims processing).']
  validation_rule varchar [note: 'Expression or constraint that validates the transformed data meets target system requirements before transmission. May include format checks, range validation, or business rule validation.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Version identifier for this mapping definition, following semantic versioning or organizational versioning standards.']

  Note: 'Master reference table for mapping_definition. Referenced by mapping_definition_id.'
}

  therapy_order_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to order.therapy_order. Business justification: Therapy sessions fulfill therapy orders. Authorization utilization tracking, billing reconciliation, and sessions-remaining calculations require linking each session to its originating therapy order.']
  utilization_review_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to insurance.utilization_review. Business justification: Payers authorize therapy in session blocks (e.g., 12 sessions). Each session must reference the UR authorization for claims submission and to track when re-authorization is needed.']
  visit_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to encounter.visit. Business justification: Inpatient therapy sessions must link to the hospital encounter for facility fee billing, length-of-stay clinical justification, and discharge planning documentation. Follows same pattern as mat_treatm']
  billing_code varchar [note: 'HCPCS code used for billing the therapy session.']
  charge_adjustment decimal(10,2) [note: 'Adjustments (discounts, write‑offs, insurance adjustments) applied to the gross charge.']
  charge_amount_gross decimal(10,2) [note: 'Total charge for the session before any adjustments.']
  charge_amount_net decimal(10,2) [note: 'Final amount payable after adjustments.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the therapy session record was first created in the system.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'Three‑letter ISO 4217 currency code for monetary amounts.']
  diagnosis_code varchar [note: 'Primary diagnosis associated with the session, using ICD‑10 coding.']
  duration_minutes varchar [note: 'Length of the session measured in whole minutes.']
  follow_up_date date [note: 'Scheduled date for the required follow‑up session, if any.']
  follow_up_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a follow‑up appointment is required after this session.']
  is_group_session boolean [note: 'True if the session involved multiple patients simultaneously.']
  is_telehealth boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the session was delivered via telehealth.']
  modality varchar [note: 'Mode of delivery for the session (in‑person individual, group, or telehealth).']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free‑text clinical documentation captured during the session.']
  outcome_measure_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Standardized numeric score reflecting patient outcome for the session (e.g., PHQ‑9 total).']
  patient_feedback varchar [note: 'Free‑text feedback provided by the patient after the session.']
  procedure_code varchar [note: 'CPT code representing the therapeutic procedure performed.']
  risk_level varchar [note: 'Clinical risk classification for the session (e.g., suicidal risk).']
  session_date date [note: 'Calendar date on which the therapy session took place.']
  session_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Exact end time of the therapy session.']
  session_number varchar [note: 'Human‑readable identifier assigned to the therapy session (e.g., TS‑20231015‑001).']
  session_outcome varchar [note: 'Clinician‑recorded overall outcome of the session.']
  session_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Exact start time of the therapy session.']

  session_type varchar [note: 'High‑level classification of the session purpose.']
  therapist_notes varchar [note: 'Additional observations recorded by the therapist.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to the therapy session record.']

  gender_criteria varchar [note: 'Gender-based eligibility filter for cohort membership. \'All\' indicates no gender restriction.']
  hipaa_minimum_necessary_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the cohort criteria and resulting patient data access comply with HIPAA minimum necessary standard.']
  inclusion_criteria_logic varchar [note: 'Structured or semi-structured expression defining the clinical, demographic, and utilization criteria patients must meet for cohort membership. May reference ICD-10, CPT, lab values, and demographic filters.']
  intervention_type varchar [note: 'Primary type of clinical intervention or outreach recommended for patients identified in this cohort.']
  irb_protocol_number varchar [note: 'IRB protocol number if this cohort is used for research purposes and requires institutional review board oversight.']
  last_refresh_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the cohort membership was last recalculated and patient lists were updated.']
  measurement_period_months varchar [note: 'Lookback window in months used to evaluate patient clinical data against cohort criteria (e.g., 12 months for annual quality measures).']
  population_cohort_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique business code assigned to this cohort for cross-system reference and reporting.']
  population_cohort_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative describing the clinical rationale, target population characteristics, and intended use of this cohort.']
  population_cohort_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable descriptive name of the population cohort (e.g., \'Diabetes Type 2 High Risk Adults 65+\').']
  population_cohort_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the cohort definition indicating whether it is actively used for patient identification and reporting.']
  priority_level varchar [note: 'Organizational priority ranking indicating urgency of intervention for this patient population.']
  program_affiliation varchar [note: 'Value-based care program or initiative this cohort supports (e.g., ACO REACH, MSSP, Bundled Payments, commercial VBP contract).']
  refresh_frequency varchar [note: 'How often the cohort membership is recalculated by evaluating patients against inclusion/exclusion criteria.']
  retention_period_months varchar [note: 'Number of months cohort membership history must be retained per regulatory and organizational data governance policy.']
  risk_model_name varchar [note: 'Name of the predictive model or algorithm used to generate risk scores for cohort stratification (e.g., \'HCC v28\', \'LACE Index\', \'Custom Readmission Model\').']
  risk_score_threshold_max decimal(5,2) [note: 'Upper bound of the AI/ML-generated risk score for cohort inclusion. Null indicates no upper limit.']
  risk_score_threshold_min decimal(5,2) [note: 'Lower bound of the AI/ML-generated risk score required for cohort inclusion. Used in risk stratification cohorts.']
  sdoh_criteria_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this cohort incorporates Social Determinants of Health factors in its inclusion or stratification criteria.']
  target_size varchar [note: 'Expected or target number of patients to be enrolled in this cohort based on population estimates.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this cohort definition record was last modified.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Sequential version number tracking revisions to the cohort inclusion/exclusion criteria over time.']

  Note: 'Population health cohort definition and membership tracking tables'
}

Table clinical_ai.model_feature_mapping {
  model_feature_mapping_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate key for the model-feature mapping record.']
  clinical_ai_feature_store_entity_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the feature definition that is consumed by the model']
  clinical_ai_model_card_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the model card that consumes this feature']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this feature-model mapping was first created.']
  effective_end_date date [note: 'Date when this feature was removed from the model\'s input feature set. NULL if currently active.']
  effective_start_date date [note: 'Date when this feature was added to the model\'s input feature set.']
  feature_version varchar [note: 'Version of the feature definition used by this specific model version.']
  importance_score decimal(6,4) [note: 'SHAP or LIME feature importance score indicating how much this feature contributes to the specific model\'s predictions. Value between 0 and 1.']
  is_active boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this feature-model mapping is currently active for production inference.']
  is_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the model requires this feature for inference or can gracefully degrade without it.']
  model_name varchar [note: 'Name of the AI/ML model that consumes this feature. [Moved from feature_store_entity: This attribute on feature_store_entity tracks which model consumes the feature, but a feature can be consumed by multiple models. This data belongs to the M:N association, not to the feature entity itself.]']
  model_version varchar [note: 'Version of the consuming model. [Moved from feature_store_entity: This attribute on feature_store_entity tracks the version of the consuming model, but since a feature can be consumed by multiple model versions simultaneously, this belongs to the association.]']
  rank varchar [note: 'Ordinal rank of this feature\'s importance within the model\'s feature set (1 = most important).']
  transformation_applied varchar [note: 'Model-specific transformation applied to the feature before model consumption (e.g., normalization, one-hot encoding, log transform).']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time of the most recent modification to this mapping.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the contractual relationship between a feature_store_entity and a model_card in clinical AI governance. It captures which features are consumed by which AI/ML models, with importance scores, version tracking, and required/optional status. Each record links one feature definition to one model card with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific feature-model relationship. This supports FDA SaMD documentation, model card governance, and MLOps feature lineage requirements.. Existence Justification: In MLOps and healthcare AI governance, the relationship between features and models is a well-established operational M:N. A single feature (e.g., patient_age, lab_value_trend) is consumed by multiple AI models simultaneously, and each model consumes multiple features as inputs. Healthcare AI governance frameworks (FDA SaMD, model cards per the user-king directive) require explicit documentation of which features each model uses, with importance scores, version tracking, and required/optional status. This is an actively managed operational relationship - data scientists and ML engineers create, update, and retire feature-model mappings as models are retrained.'
}

Table clinical_ai.criteria_match_evaluation {
  criteria_match_evaluation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Surrogate primary key for each criteria match evaluation record']
  clinical_ai_clinical_nlp_result_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the NLP extraction result that provides clinical evidence for the eligibility criterion evaluation']
  eligibility_criteria_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the trial eligibility criterion being evaluated against the NLP extraction']
  criteria_met_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the eligibility criterion is considered satisfied by this NLP extraction based on the match evaluation']
  evaluation_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this match evaluation was performed or last updated']
  match_score decimal(5,4) [note: 'Confidence score (0.0 to 1.0) indicating how strongly the NLP extraction satisfies the eligibility criterion']
  match_status varchar [note: 'Current evaluation status of this NLP-to-criterion match as determined by the trial coordinator or automated system']

  Note: 'This association product represents the evaluation event between a clinical NLP extraction result and a trial eligibility criterion. It captures whether a specific NLP-extracted clinical concept satisfies a specific trial eligibility requirement, with match confidence scoring and evaluation status tracking. Each record links one clinical_nlp_result to one eligibility_criteria with attributes that exist only in the context of this matching relationship. Trial coordinators actively manage these evaluations as part of the clinical trial screening and patient matching workflow.. Existence Justification: In clinical trial matching workflows, trial coordinators actively evaluate NLP-extracted clinical concepts (e.g., HbA1c=8.2, diabetes diagnosis) against trial eligibility criteria. One NLP extraction can satisfy criteria across multiple trials simultaneously, and one eligibility criterion (e.g., \'must have Type 2 diabetes\') can be evidenced by multiple NLP extractions from different patient notes. This is an operational process where coordinators actively create, review, and update match evaluations as part of the clinical trial screening workflow.'
}

Table clinical_ai.model_tag_assignment {
  model_tag_assignment_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate key for the model tag assignment record']
  clinical_ai_model_card_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the AI model card that is being tagged for governance classification']
  uc_tag_definition_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the Unity Catalog tag definition being applied to the model']
  applied_by varchar [note: 'Identity of the user or service principal who applied the tag to the model, required for HIPAA audit compliance']
  applied_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date-time when the tag was applied to the model card, supporting governance audit trail']
  is_inherited boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the tag was inherited from a parent model or catalog-level policy rather than explicitly assigned to this model card']
  tag_value decimal(18,2) [note: 'The specific value assigned from the tag definition\'s allowed_values list (e.g., \'true\', \'high\', \'cardiology\')']

  Note: 'This association product represents the governance assignment of Unity Catalog tag definitions to AI model cards. It captures which tags are applied to which models, the specific tag values, who applied them, and when — supporting HIPAA compliance audits, dynamic data masking policy enforcement, and clinical AI governance workflows. Each record links one model_card to one uc_tag_definition with attributes that exist only in the context of this tagging relationship.. Existence Justification: In healthcare AI governance, one AI model (model_card) requires multiple Unity Catalog tag definitions (PHI, PII, risk_tier, department, sensitivity level) to properly classify its inputs and outputs for HIPAA compliance. Conversely, one tag definition (e.g., pii_phi) applies to many AI models across the organization. Healthcare data governance teams actively manage these tag assignments as part of model deployment workflows, tracking who applied each tag, when, and what value was assigned.'
}

Table clinical_ai.feature_tag_application {
  feature_tag_application_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the feature_tag_application association']
  clinical_ai_feature_store_entity_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the feature store entity being tagged']
  uc_tag_definition_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the Unity Catalog tag definition being applied']
  applied_by varchar [note: 'Identity of the data steward or automated process that applied this tag to the feature, required for HIPAA audit trail.']
  applied_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this tag was applied to the feature entity, supporting audit trail for governance changes.']
  is_sensitive_override boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this specific tag application overrides the default sensitivity classification derived from the tag definition, allowing per-feature exceptions to standard governance rules.']
  tag_value decimal(18,2) [note: 'The specific value assigned for this tag on this feature entity. For boolean tags like pii_phi this is true/false; for categorical tags like sensitivity_level this is the level.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the application of Unity Catalog tag definitions to feature store entities for PHI/PII classification and governance. Each record links one feature_store_entity to one uc_tag_definition with the specific tag value assigned, who applied it, and when. This enables dynamic data masking, row-level security policies, and HIPAA compliance auditing across the clinical AI feature store.. Existence Justification: In a Databricks healthcare lakehouse, feature store entities (ML features derived from clinical data) require multiple Unity Catalog tag classifications (pii_phi, pii_pii, pii_sensitive, data_domain, sensitivity_level) simultaneously, and each tag definition applies to hundreds or thousands of features across the catalog. This is an operational governance relationship that data stewards actively manage - they apply, modify, and revoke tag assignments as features change sensitivity classification. The relationship itself carries data (tag_value, applied_timestamp, applied_by, is_sensitive_override) that belongs to neither the feature nor the tag definition alone.'
}

Table digital_health.program_monitoring_requirement {
  program_monitoring_requirement_id varchar [pk, note: 'System-generated unique identifier for the program monitoring requirement record.']
  rpm_program_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the RPM program that defines this monitoring requirement']
  test_catalog_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the laboratory test catalog entry required by the program']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this monitoring requirement record was created.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date when this test requirement became active for the RPM program. Supports versioning of program protocols over time.']
  end_date date [note: 'Date when this test requirement was retired or superseded within the RPM program. Null indicates currently active requirement.']
  frequency_requirement varchar [note: 'How often the test must be performed within the program (e.g., weekly, monthly, quarterly). Defines the clinical protocol cadence for this specific test within this specific program.']
  is_mandatory boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this lab test is mandatory (true) or optional/recommended (false) for patients enrolled in the RPM program.']
  monitoring_interval_days varchar [note: 'Number of days between required test administrations for this program-test combination. Provides numeric precision for scheduling and compliance tracking.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this monitoring requirement record was last modified.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the contractual requirement between an RPM program and a laboratory test catalog entry. It captures which lab tests are required or recommended for each remote patient monitoring program, along with the frequency, interval, and mandatory/optional status of each test within the program. Each record links one RPM program to one test catalog entry with attributes that exist only in the context of this monitoring protocol relationship.. Existence Justification: RPM programs define required laboratory monitoring protocols where one diabetes RPM program requires multiple lab tests (HbA1c, BMP, lipid panel) and one lab test like HbA1c serves multiple RPM programs (diabetes management, cardiovascular risk, pre-surgical optimization). Healthcare organizations actively manage these program-test associations with specific frequency requirements, mandatory/optional designations, and effective date ranges that belong to neither the program nor the test alone.'
}

Table genomics.variant_interpretation {
  variant_interpretation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for variant_interpretation']
  genomic_test_order_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the laboratory or genomic test order that produced the variant data being interpreted.']
  mpi_record_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the patient for whom the variant interpretation was performed.']
  variant_clinician_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the provider who ordered the genomic test leading to this interpretation.']
  variant_interpreting_provider_clinician_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the clinical geneticist or molecular pathologist who performed the variant interpretation.']
  visit_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the clinical encounter during which the genomic test was ordered or results were reviewed.']
  acmg_classification varchar [note: 'Five-tier clinical significance classification per ACMG/AMP guidelines: pathogenic, likely pathogenic, variant of uncertain significance (VUS), likely benign, or benign.']
  allele_frequency decimal(10,8) [note: 'Minor allele frequency of the variant in the general population from gnomAD or similar population databases, used to assess rarity.']
  amended_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent amendment to the interpretation report, if applicable.']
  amendment_reason varchar [note: 'Explanation for why the variant interpretation report was amended after initial finalization.']
  associated_condition varchar [note: 'Primary clinical condition or disease phenotype associated with the interpreted variant (e.g., Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer Syndrome).']
  chromosome varchar [note: 'Chromosome on which the variant is located (e.g., chr17, chrX).']
  clia_lab_number varchar [note: 'CLIA certification number of the performing laboratory, required for regulatory compliance of clinical genomic testing.']
  clinical_significance_summary varchar [note: 'Free-text narrative summarizing the clinical significance of the variant in the context of the patient\'s phenotype and family history.']
  clinvar_accession varchar [note: 'ClinVar submission accession number linking this interpretation to the NCBI ClinVar public archive of variant-disease relationships.']
  computational_score decimal(6,4) [note: 'Numeric pathogenicity score from the primary computational prediction tool used (e.g., CADD PHRED score, REVEL score).']
  computational_tool_used varchar [note: 'Name and version of the primary computational prediction tool used to generate the pathogenicity score (e.g., CADD v1.6, REVEL, AlphaMissense).']
  cosmic_accession varchar [note: 'COSMIC identifier for somatic variants found in cancer genomes, applicable to tumor-related interpretations.']
  dbsnp_rsid varchar [note: 'dbSNP reference SNP cluster identifier (rsID) for the variant, enabling cross-referencing with public genomic databases.']
  evidence_criteria_applied varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of ACMG/AMP evidence criteria codes applied to reach the classification (e.g., PVS1, PM2, PP3).']
  family_segregation_data varchar [note: 'Summary of family segregation analysis data indicating whether the variant co-segregates with disease in affected family members.']
  functional_impact_prediction varchar [note: 'Consensus in silico prediction of functional impact from computational tools such as SIFT, PolyPhen-2, CADD, or REVEL.']
  gene_symbol varchar [note: 'Official HGNC-approved gene symbol for the gene in which the variant was identified (e.g., BRCA1, TP53, EGFR).']
  genetic_counseling_recommended boolean [note: 'Indicates whether genetic counseling is recommended for the patient and/or family members based on this interpretation.']
  genomic_position varchar [note: 'Genomic coordinate position of the variant on the reference genome assembly.']
  hgvs_coding_notation varchar [note: 'HGVS-formatted coding DNA sequence notation describing the variant at the nucleotide level (e.g., c.5266dupC).']
  hgvs_protein_notation varchar [note: 'HGVS-formatted protein-level notation describing the predicted amino acid change (e.g., p.Gln1756ProfsTer74).']
  inheritance_pattern varchar [note: 'Mode of inheritance for the condition associated with the variant.']
  interpretation_date date [note: 'Date on which the clinical variant interpretation was completed and signed by the interpreting provider.']
  interpretation_status varchar [note: 'Current state of the variant interpretation report in its clinical workflow lifecycle.']
  interpretation_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the type of genomic variant interpretation being performed (germline hereditary, somatic tumor, pharmacogenomic, prenatal, or carrier screening).']
  is_actionable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the variant interpretation has direct clinical actionability (e.g., changes management, qualifies for targeted therapy, or triggers surveillance recommendations).']
  is_reportable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this variant meets criteria for inclusion in the clinical report to the ordering provider (true = reportable, false = not reported).']
  is_secondary_finding boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this variant represents an ACMG-recommended secondary finding unrelated to the primary test indication.']
  performing_laboratory_name varchar [note: 'Name of the CLIA-certified laboratory that performed the genomic sequencing and initial variant calling.']
  population_database_source varchar [note: 'Reference population database from which the allele frequency was obtained.']
  read_depth varchar [note: 'Total number of sequencing reads covering the variant position, indicating confidence in the variant call.']
  reference_genome_build varchar [note: 'Human reference genome assembly version used for variant coordinate mapping.']
  report_issued_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the finalized variant interpretation report was officially issued and made available to the ordering provider.']
  report_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique report number assigned to this variant interpretation report for clinical tracking and communication.']
  review_notes varchar [note: 'Internal notes from the variant review board or molecular tumor board discussion regarding this interpretation.']
  specimen_type varchar [note: 'Type of biological specimen from which the genomic DNA was extracted for sequencing.']
  test_methodology varchar [note: 'Laboratory methodology used to detect the variant (whole genome sequencing, whole exome sequencing, targeted gene panel, single gene test, FISH, or array CGH). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WGS|WES|targeted_panel|single_gene|FISH|array_CGH|RNA_seq — promote to reference product]']
  test_panel_name varchar [note: 'Name of the specific gene panel or test assay used (e.g., Comprehensive Cancer Panel, Hereditary Cardiac Panel).']
  therapeutic_implication varchar [note: 'Summary of therapeutic implications including targeted therapy eligibility, drug sensitivity or resistance, and clinical trial candidacy based on the variant.']
  tier_classification varchar [note: 'Four-tier classification for somatic variants per AMP/ASCO/CAP guidelines indicating level of clinical evidence for actionability. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tier_I_A|tier_I_B|tier_II_C|tier_II_D|tier_III|tier_IV — promote to reference product]']
  tumor_mutational_burden decimal(8,2) [note: 'Tumor mutational burden measured in mutations per megabase, relevant for somatic variant interpretations and immunotherapy eligibility assessment.']
  variant_allele_fraction decimal(5,4) [note: 'Proportion of sequencing reads supporting the variant allele at this position, indicating clonality in somatic contexts or confirming zygosity in germline contexts.']
  variant_class varchar [note: 'Structural classification of the genomic variant (single nucleotide variant, insertion, deletion, indel, copy number variant, or structural variant).']
  zygosity varchar [note: 'Zygosity state of the variant in the patient (heterozygous, homozygous, hemizygous, or compound heterozygous).']

  Note: 'Variant interpretation reports'
}

  is_incidental_finding boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this variant is a secondary or incidental finding unrelated to the primary indication for testing.']

  panel_name varchar [note: 'Name of the targeted gene panel used for sequencing, if applicable (e.g., FoundationOne CDx, Tempus xT).']
  position_end varchar [note: 'End position of the variant on the chromosome; equals position_start for single nucleotide variants.']
  position_start varchar [note: 'Start position of the variant on the chromosome in 1-based coordinate system.']

  read_depth varchar [note: 'Total number of sequencing reads covering the variant position, indicating confidence in the call.']
  reference_allele varchar [note: 'Reference genome allele at the variant position, expressed in standard nucleotide notation.']

  somatic_or_germline varchar [note: 'Classification of whether the variant is of somatic (tumor-acquired) or germline (inherited) origin.']
  therapeutic_implication varchar [note: 'Summary of therapeutic implications including drug sensitivity, resistance, or eligibility for targeted therapy based on this variant.']
  transcript_accession varchar [note: 'RefSeq or Ensembl transcript identifier used as the reference for variant annotation.']

  number_of_lanes varchar [note: 'Total number of lanes on the flow cell utilized in this sequencing run.']
  output_folder_path varchar [note: 'File system or cloud storage path where the raw sequencing output (BCL/FASTQ files) is stored.']
  percent_aligned_phix decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of reads aligned to the PhiX control genome, used for quality monitoring and error rate estimation.']
  percent_clusters_passing_filter decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of clusters that pass the quality filter, indicating the proportion of usable data from the run.']
  percent_q30 decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of bases with a quality score of Q30 or higher, indicating the proportion of high-confidence base calls.']
  percent_undetermined_reads decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of reads that could not be assigned to a sample during demultiplexing, indicating index hopping or contamination.']
  platform varchar [note: 'The sequencing technology platform used for this run, indicating the underlying chemistry and detection method.']
  qc_status varchar [note: 'Quality control assessment outcome for the sequencing run, determining whether data meets release criteria.']
  read_configuration varchar [note: 'Configuration of the sequencing reads (e.g., 2x150, 1x100, 2x250), specifying paired-end or single-end and read lengths.']
  read_length varchar [note: 'The configured read length in base pairs for this sequencing run, determining the length of each sequenced fragment.']
  reagent_kit_expiration_date date [note: 'Expiration date of the reagent kit used, relevant for compliance and quality assurance.']
  reagent_kit_lot_number varchar [note: 'Lot number of the reagent kit used for this sequencing run, supporting supply chain traceability and quality investigations.']
  run_duration_hours decimal(6,2) [note: 'Total elapsed time of the sequencing run in hours from start to completion.']
  run_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the sequencing run completed or was terminated on the instrument.']
  run_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name or label assigned to the sequencing run, typically following laboratory naming conventions for identification and tracking purposes.']
  run_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique business identifier for the sequencing run, used for cross-system reference and laboratory tracking.']
  run_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the sequencing run was initiated on the instrument.']
  run_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the sequencing run by the type of genomic assay or application being performed.']
  sequencing_run_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the sequencing run, tracking its progression from planning through completion or failure.']
  total_bases_generated varchar [note: 'Total number of bases (nucleotides) sequenced in this run, representing overall data yield.']
  total_reads_generated varchar [note: 'Total number of sequencing reads generated by this run, a primary throughput metric.']
  total_samples varchar [note: 'Total number of samples (libraries) loaded onto this sequencing run.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this sequencing run record was last modified.']

  Note: 'Table storing sequencing run metadata.'
}

  reference_genome varchar [note: 'The human reference genome assembly version used for read alignment and variant calling.']
  sample_collection_date date [note: 'Date when the biological sample was collected from the patient.']

  sequencing_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the genomic sequencing methodology used for this run.']
  tissue_source varchar [note: 'Anatomical site or tissue type from which the sample was obtained (e.g., blood, bone marrow, lung biopsy).']
  total_reads varchar [note: 'Total number of raw sequencing reads generated for this sample in this run.']
  total_yield_gb decimal(10,2) [note: 'Total sequencing data yield in gigabases generated for this sample.']
  tumor_purity_percent decimal(5,2) [note: 'Estimated percentage of tumor cells in the sample, critical for somatic variant calling sensitivity in oncology.']

  library_prep_method varchar [note: 'Method used for sequencing library preparation (e.g., PCR-based, hybrid capture, amplicon-based), which affects coverage uniformity and bias.']
  mapped_reads_percent decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of total reads that successfully aligned to the reference genome, indicating data quality.']
  mean_coverage_depth decimal(10,2) [note: 'Average number of times each nucleotide position in the target region was sequenced. Higher coverage improves variant calling confidence.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes from laboratory staff or bioinformaticians regarding the sequencing run, specimen handling, or analysis observations.']
  on_target_percent decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of reads that map to the intended target regions for panel or exome sequencing, indicating capture efficiency.']
  order_date date [note: 'Date when the genomic sequencing test was ordered by the provider.']
  overall_result_classification varchar [note: 'High-level classification of the sequencing result indicating whether clinically actionable findings were identified.']
  panel_name varchar [note: 'Name of the targeted gene panel used for sequencing, if applicable (e.g., Oncology 500 Gene Panel, Hereditary Cancer Panel).']
  platform varchar [note: 'The sequencing instrument platform used to generate the data (e.g., Illumina NovaSeq, PacBio Sequel, Oxford Nanopore). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: illumina_novaseq|illumina_hiseq|illumina_miseq|pacbio_sequel|oxford_nanopore|ion_torrent|bgi_dnbseq — promote to reference product]']
  q30_percent decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of bases with a Phred quality score of 30 or higher (99.9% base call accuracy), a key quality metric for sequencing data.']
  quality_control_status varchar [note: 'Outcome of quality control assessment for the sequencing run, determining whether results meet minimum quality thresholds for clinical reporting.']
  read_length_bp varchar [note: 'Length of individual sequencing reads in base pairs, which impacts alignment accuracy and variant detection sensitivity.']
  reference_genome varchar [note: 'Human reference genome assembly version used for alignment and variant calling (e.g., GRCh38 is the current standard).']

  run_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the sequencing instrument run began processing the specimen.']
  sample_type varchar [note: 'Type of biological sample from which DNA/RNA was extracted for sequencing.']
  sequencing_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the genomic sequencing workflow from order through completion or failure.']
  sequencing_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the genomic sequencing methodology used. WGS=Whole Genome Sequencing, WES=Whole Exome Sequencing, targeted_panel=Gene Panel, RNA_seq=RNA Sequencing.']
  storage_location_uri varchar [note: 'Uniform Resource Identifier pointing to the cloud or on-premises storage location of the raw and processed sequencing data files.']
  total_reads varchar [note: 'Total number of sequencing reads generated during the run for this specimen.']

Table genomics.variant_call {
  variant_call_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for variant_call']
  care_site_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the laboratory or genomics facility that performed the sequencing and variant calling.']
  genomic_test_order_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the clinical genomic test order that initiated the sequencing workflow producing this variant call.']
  mpi_record_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the patient from whom the genomic specimen was collected and sequenced.']
  specimen_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the biological specimen (e.g., blood, tissue, saliva) from which DNA was extracted for sequencing.']
  variant_clinician_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the clinician who ordered the genomic test that produced this variant call.']
  variant_interpreting_pathologist_clinician_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the molecular pathologist or clinical geneticist who performed the clinical interpretation and classification.']

  acmg_criteria varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of ACMG/AMP evidence criteria codes applied during variant classification (e.g., PVS1, PM2, PP3).']
  actionability_category varchar [note: 'AMP/ASCO/CAP tier classification indicating the level of clinical actionability for somatic variants in oncology contexts.']
  allele_frequency decimal(7,6) [note: 'Fraction of sequencing reads supporting the alternate allele relative to total reads at this position (0.0 to 1.0).']
  alternate_allele varchar [note: 'Observed variant nucleotide sequence differing from the reference allele at this genomic position.']
  alternate_allele_depth varchar [note: 'Number of sequencing reads supporting the alternate allele at this position.']
  assay_type varchar [note: 'Type of genomic assay performed: whole genome sequencing (WGS), whole exome sequencing (WES), targeted gene panel, or other methodology.']
  associated_condition varchar [note: 'Primary disease or clinical condition associated with this variant based on curated evidence (e.g., ClinVar condition, OMIM phenotype).']
  call_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the variant calling pipeline completed analysis and generated this variant call record.']
  chromosome varchar [note: 'Chromosome on which the variant is located, using standard nomenclature (e.g., chr1 through chr22, chrX, chrY, chrM). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: chr1|chr2|chr3|chr4|chr5|chr6|chr7|chr8|chr9|chr10|chr11|chr12|chr13|chr14|chr15|chr16|chr17|chr18|chr19|chr20|chr21|chr22|chrX|chrY|chrM — promote to reference product]']
  clinical_significance varchar [note: 'Clinical interpretation of the variant\'s pathogenicity according to ACMG/AMP five-tier classification guidelines.']
  clinvar_accession varchar [note: 'NCBI ClinVar database variation identifier linking this variant to curated clinical significance assertions.']
  cosmic_accession varchar [note: 'Catalogue of Somatic Mutations in Cancer (COSMIC) identifier for somatic variants relevant to oncology.']
  dbsnp_accession varchar [note: 'NCBI dbSNP reference SNP cluster identifier for this variant, enabling cross-referencing with public variant databases.']
  end_position varchar [note: '1-based coordinate of the end position of the variant on the reference genome, relevant for structural variants and indels spanning multiple bases.']
  filter_status varchar [note: 'Result of quality filtering applied to the variant call indicating whether it passed all quality thresholds or was flagged for specific issues.']
  functional_consequence varchar [note: 'Predicted functional effect of the variant on the gene product (e.g., missense, nonsense, frameshift). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: missense|nonsense|frameshift|splice_site|synonymous|intronic|UTR|intergenic|stop_gain|stop_loss|inframe_insertion|inframe_deletion — promote to reference product]']
  gene_symbol varchar [note: 'HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (HGNC) approved gene symbol in which the variant is located or nearest to.']
  genomic_position varchar [note: '1-based coordinate position of the variant on the reference genome assembly, indicating the start position of the variant.']
  genotype varchar [note: 'Genotype call for this variant position expressed in VCF format (e.g., 0/1 for heterozygous, 1/1 for homozygous alternate).']
  hgvs_coding varchar [note: 'Human Genome Variation Society (HGVS) nomenclature for the variant at the coding DNA level (c. notation).']
  hgvs_protein varchar [note: 'Human Genome Variation Society (HGVS) nomenclature for the predicted protein-level change (p. notation).']
  inheritance_pattern varchar [note: 'Mode of inheritance associated with the variant\'s linked condition, relevant for genetic counseling and family cascade testing.']
  interpretation_status varchar [note: 'Current status of clinical interpretation workflow for this variant call, tracking progress from detection through final reporting.']
  interpretation_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the clinical interpretation and classification of this variant was finalized by the molecular pathologist.']
  is_incidental_finding boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this variant is an incidental or secondary finding unrelated to the primary indication for testing, per ACMG SF list.']
  is_reportable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this variant meets criteria for inclusion in the clinical genomic report delivered to the ordering provider.']
  pipeline_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the complete bioinformatics analysis pipeline used for alignment, variant calling, and annotation.']
  population_allele_frequency decimal(10,8) [note: 'Frequency of this variant allele in the general population from gnomAD or similar population databases, used for rarity assessment.']
  quality_score decimal(10,2) [note: 'Phred-scaled quality score representing the confidence that the variant call is genuine and not a sequencing artifact.']
  read_depth varchar [note: 'Total number of sequencing reads covering this genomic position, indicating the depth of coverage supporting the variant call.']
  reference_allele varchar [note: 'Nucleotide sequence at this position in the reference genome assembly (e.g., A, C, G, T, or multi-base for indels).']
  reference_genome_build varchar [note: 'Version of the human reference genome assembly used for alignment and variant calling (e.g., GRCh37/hg19, GRCh38/hg38).']
  reported_date date [note: 'Date when this variant was included in a finalized clinical genomic report released to the ordering provider.']
  review_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text clinical notes documenting the rationale for variant classification, evidence reviewed, and any caveats noted during interpretation.']
  sequencing_platform varchar [note: 'Technology platform used for DNA sequencing that generated the raw reads from which this variant was called.']
  somatic_germline_status varchar [note: 'Classification of whether the variant originated in somatic (tumor) tissue or is present in the germline (inherited), critical for treatment decisions.']
  strand_bias_score decimal(8,4) [note: 'Statistical measure of strand bias indicating whether the variant is supported equally by forward and reverse reads, used as a quality metric.']
  therapeutic_implication varchar [note: 'Summary of treatment implications including drug sensitivity, resistance, or eligibility for targeted therapy based on this variant.']
  transcript_accession varchar [note: 'RefSeq or Ensembl transcript identifier used for annotation of the variant\'s functional impact.']
  variant_caller varchar [note: 'Name and version of the bioinformatics variant calling software used to identify this variant (e.g., GATK HaplotypeCaller 4.3, DeepVariant 1.5).']
  variant_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the genomic variant by structural category: single nucleotide variant (SNV), insertion, deletion, indel, multi-nucleotide variant (MNV), or copy number variant (CNV).']
  zygosity varchar [note: 'Allelic state of the variant in the patient\'s genome indicating whether one or both allele copies carry the variant.']

  Note: 'genomics.variant_call'
}

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: missense|nonsense|frameshift|splice_site|synonymous|intronic|in_frame_deletion|in_frame_insertion|start_loss|stop_loss — promote to reference product]']
  gene_symbol varchar [note: 'Official HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (HGNC) approved gene symbol where the variant is located (e.g., BRCA1, EGFR, TP53).']

  genomic_position_start varchar [note: 'Start position of the variant on the chromosome in the reference genome coordinate system.']

  hgvs_protein varchar [note: 'HGVS nomenclature for the predicted protein change (p. notation), describing the amino acid alteration.']
  incidental_finding_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this variant is an incidental or secondary finding unrelated to the primary test indication, per ACMG SF guidelines.']

  interpretation_date date [note: 'Date when the clinical interpretation and significance classification were finalized by the reviewing pathologist.']
  interpretation_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text clinical notes from the interpreting pathologist providing additional context, evidence citations, or caveats about the variant classification.']
  interpretation_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the clinical interpretation for this variant result within the reporting workflow.']
  loinc_code varchar [note: 'LOINC code representing the specific genomic observation or test result for interoperability and standardized reporting.']
  panel_name varchar [note: 'Name of the specific gene panel or test assay used if the methodology is a targeted panel approach.']
  population_frequency decimal(10,8) [note: 'Frequency of the alternate allele in the general population from gnomAD or similar population databases, used to assess rarity.']
  quality_score decimal(8,2) [note: 'Phred-scaled quality score representing the confidence that the variant call is correct.']
  read_depth varchar [note: 'Total number of sequencing reads covering the variant position, indicating the confidence level of the variant call.']
  reference_allele varchar [note: 'The nucleotide sequence at the variant position in the reference genome assembly.']
  reference_genome_build varchar [note: 'The human reference genome assembly version used for alignment and variant calling (e.g., GRCh37/hg19, GRCh38/hg38).']
  report_date date [note: 'Date when the final genomic variant report was issued and made available to the ordering provider.']
  reportable_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this variant meets criteria for inclusion in the final clinical report to the ordering provider.']
  result_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the variant result was first generated by the bioinformatics pipeline or laboratory system.']
  somatic_germline_flag varchar [note: 'Classification of whether the variant is somatic (acquired in tumor) or germline (inherited), critical for treatment decisions.']
  specimen_collection_date date [note: 'Date when the biological specimen was collected from the patient for genomic testing.']
  specimen_type varchar [note: 'Type of biological specimen from which DNA was extracted for genomic sequencing.']
  test_methodology varchar [note: 'The genomic testing methodology used to detect this variant (e.g., whole genome sequencing, whole exome sequencing, targeted gene panel).']
  therapeutic_implication varchar [note: 'Summary of therapeutic implications of the variant, including associated targeted therapies, drug sensitivity, or resistance information.']
  transcript_accession varchar [note: 'RefSeq or Ensembl transcript identifier used as the reference for coding and protein-level annotations.']
  tumor_normal_indicator varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the variant was detected from a tumor-only analysis, paired tumor-normal comparison, or germline testing.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this genomic variant result record was last modified or updated.']
  variant_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the type of genomic variant detected (e.g., single nucleotide variant, insertion, deletion, copy number variant, structural variant).']
  zygosity varchar [note: 'The zygosity state of the variant in the patient sample, indicating whether one or both alleles carry the variant.']

  Note: 'Table for genomic variant results.'
}

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: poor_metabolizer|intermediate_metabolizer|normal_metabolizer|rapid_metabolizer|ultrarapid_metabolizer|indeterminate|likely_poor|likely_intermediate — promote to reference product]']
  population_frequency decimal(7,4) [note: 'Frequency of the identified allele or diplotype in the general population or relevant ethnic subpopulation, used for clinical context.']

  sample_adequacy varchar [note: 'Assessment of whether the submitted specimen met minimum quality and quantity requirements for successful genomic analysis.']
  sequencing_platform varchar [note: 'Technology platform used for genomic sequencing (e.g., Illumina NovaSeq, Ion Torrent, Oxford Nanopore).']
  specimen_collection_date date [note: 'Date when the biological specimen was collected from the patient for genomic testing.']
  specimen_site varchar [note: 'Anatomical site from which the specimen was obtained, coded per SNOMED CT body structure hierarchy.']
  specimen_type varchar [note: 'Type of biological specimen used for genomic analysis, such as tissue biopsy, blood draw, saliva, bone marrow, cell-free DNA, or formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue.']
  test_code varchar [note: 'Standardized code identifying the genomic test, typically mapped to CPT or proprietary lab codes.']
  test_name varchar [note: 'Name of the specific genomic test or panel performed (e.g., FoundationOne CDx, Tempus xT, Guardant360).']
  therapy_match_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the genomic profile identified at least one FDA-approved or NCCN-recommended targeted therapy option.']
  total_variant_count varchar [note: 'Total number of genomic variants detected across all significance tiers in this profile.']
  tumor_mutational_burden decimal(10,2) [note: 'Number of somatic mutations per megabase of sequenced DNA, used as a biomarker for immunotherapy response prediction.']
  tumor_purity_percent decimal(5,2) [note: 'Estimated percentage of tumor cells in the specimen, critical for variant allele frequency interpretation and analytical sensitivity.']
  tumor_type varchar [note: 'Specific tumor or disease classification relevant to the genomic profile, typically aligned with oncology nomenclature.']
  turnaround_days varchar [note: 'Number of calendar days from specimen receipt at the lab to final report issuance.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the genomic profile record was last modified.']

  Note: 'Genomic Profile table'
}

Table genomics.genomic_cohort_qualification {
  genomic_cohort_qualification_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate key for the genomic cohort qualification record']
  genomics_patient_genomic_profile_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the patient genomic profile that qualified for the cohort']
  population_health_cohort_mgmt_cohort_definition_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the cohort definition the profile qualified for']
  genomic_risk_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Risk score calculated in the context of this specific cohort qualification, derived from the genomic profile data']
  inclusion_confidence decimal(5,4) [note: 'Confidence level (0-1) that the genomic profile truly meets the cohort inclusion criteria']
  qualification_criteria_met varchar [note: 'Specific inclusion criteria from the cohort definition that this genomic profile satisfies']
  qualification_date date [note: 'Date when the patient genomic profile was determined to qualify for the cohort']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Qualification event between patient_genomic_profile and cohort_definition. It captures the operational record of a patient\'s genomic profile meeting the inclusion criteria for a population health cohort. Each record links one patient_genomic_profile to one cohort_definition with attributes that exist only in the context of this qualification relationship, including when the qualification occurred, which criteria were met, the genomic risk score in context, and the confidence of inclusion.. Existence Justification: In precision medicine and population health management, a single patient\'s genomic profile qualifies them for multiple cohorts simultaneously (e.g., BRCA1+ cohort, high pharmacogenomic risk cohort, hereditary cancer cohort), and each cohort definition includes many patients with different genomic profiles. Healthcare organizations actively manage these qualifications as part of clinical trial matching, targeted intervention programs, and population health stratification. The relationship \'Genomic Cohort Qualification\' is an operational entity that clinicians and research coordinators create, review, and update.'
}

  genomics_patient_genomic_profile_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the patient genomic profile that qualified for cohort inclusion']
